**Test image observations:**
- Green sugarcane leaf with a distinct reddish-maroon/burgundy streak running along the midrib area
- The lamina (leaf blade) on both sides of the midrib remains green
- The streak is elongated, following the leaf axis — not discrete spots

**Reference image comparison (Yellow_Leaf - LeafNet_136):**
- Shows advanced Yellow Leaf: entire leaf turned yellow/golden with dark midrib streaking
- The test image appears to be an earlier/different stage — the leaf is still green but the midrib shows the characteristic reddish discoloration

**Reasoning:**
- Yellow Leaf disease (Sugarcane Yellow Leaf Virus) classically presents with **midrib reddening/yellowing** on an otherwise green leaf in early stages, progressing to complete leaf yellowing
- The reddish-maroon midrib on a predominantly green leaf matches the early symptom profile of Yellow Leaf
- Other candidates: Leaf_Scald typically shows white/cream pencil-line streaks (not reddish); Streak_Mosaic shows yellow-green streaks across the blade; Brown_Spot shows discrete oval spots — none fit as well
- The elongated midrib-specific streak on a green background is the hallmark early sign of Yellow Leaf syndrome
